title: Repetitive spinal magnetic stimulation to improve arm function after stroke (spinal-MAST)
summary:
After damage of the tractus cortico-spinalis, e.g. after stroke patients suffer from paresis of the arm and leg. The severity of the paresis depends on the amount of the damage to the pyramidal tract.
Regular physical therapy and occupational therapy facilitates improvement based on neuroplasticity of the brain.     
Non-invasive brain stimulation, such as repetitive transcranial stimulation (rTMS), applied in addition to physical and occupational therapy can force functional improvement (Hummels et al., 2005). It is known that at the spinal level, the pyramidal pathway is switched in the second motoneuron of the anterior horn (cornu anterius).The aim of repetitive spinal stimulation is to stimulate the gray matter at the spinal level, in contrast to transcranial magnetic stimulation, which stimulates the gray matter of the brain. 
In a randomized controlled trial in healthy subjects, spinal stimulation combined with motor skill training showed similar training effect (all groups completed the same motor training) in comparison to rTMS and anodal tDCS (transcranial direct current stimulation) (Wieduwild et al., unpublished data). This indicates that spinal stimulation supports neuroplastic processes. 
This randomized controlled trial aims to test the efficacy of spinal stimulation (Spin-Stim) in patients with ACM infarction with arm plegia - arm paresis compared to usual neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES). The hypothesis is that additional spinal stimulation will lead to a better effect of arm function compared to NMES (superiority study).
conditions: Sequelae of stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction

interventions.name: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation with a duration of 10min, 4 days per week for 4 weeks
spinal stimulation with a duration of 10min, apllied 4 days in the week for a 4 week period

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
First ever stroke
stroke onset between 7 days and 6 months 
plegia or paresis of the arm
ability to consent is given
Exclusion criteria:
Another stroke occurrence in the past
affection of the central nervious system except current stroke (e.g. intracranial bleeding, Multiple sklerosis, brain trauma, etc.)
